precepts.text: In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan: the language of Canaan is referring to the scriptures. In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt: it is talking about where the Israelites are, here in Babylon the great, the spiritual Egypt. And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them. Who is that saviour? Christ.
precepts.point: Who art thou, O great mountain? Remember, Zerubbabel was in the Persian captivity; Babylon was already destroyed by Persia. So this great mountain is Babylon to come: Babylon the great. Does everybody understand that?
precepts.why:
Zechariah says Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who is the headstone? Christ. Why are they crying grace, grace? Isaiah shows it, and shows that Zerubbabel is in these last days as well: “In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the Lord of hosts; one shall be called, The city of destruction.”

The language of Canaan is the scriptures, and one city shall be destroyed. “In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the Lord.” An altar is for sacrifice, and this is talking about where the Israelites are: here in Babylon the great.

“And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them.” Who is that saviour? Christ.

So Zechariah is saying the same thing. The headstone is that saviour we just read about in Isaiah, and the crying of grace, grace is because of the oppressor. The great mountain, Babylon the great, becomes a plain before him, and he delivers his people out of the land where they cried.

precepts.text: The burden of Egypt: this Egypt is Babylon the Great, like we read in Revelation 11:8. I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: that's civil war, everyone against his brother, city against city, kingdom against kingdom. Don't be surprised if it's blue states against red states, Democrats against Republicans, and everybody picks a side. And the Egyptians will I give over into the hand of a cruel lord; and a fierce king shall rule over them.
precepts.point: Video played on Agenda 21: a master plan to change the political and economic system of the world to total collectivism. People must be dependent on the state for everything; they cannot have private property or land of their own; they are to live in high-rise apartments provided as a benefit, because anybody with a couple of acres, his own water supply, and his own food is a threat to a collectivist society. You see BlackRock and Blackstone buying up housing across America, trying to get rid of private homes. It correlates to what happened in Egypt in Genesis 47: give us food, take care of us, and we give up our property and become servants. You don't think that will happen again? The things written aforetime were written for our learning.
precepts.why:
“The burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt in the midst of it.” This Egypt is Babylon the Great, the same great city of Revelation 11:8, spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.

“And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.” That is civil war. Don't be surprised if it is blue states against red states, Democrats against Republicans, and everybody picks a side. Already the government is paying the January 6th rioters, over a riot in which five people died.

“And the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof”: that great American battle cry shall fail. “and I will destroy the counsel thereof: and they shall seek to the idols, and to the charmers, and to them that have familiar spirits, and to the wizards.”

“And the Egyptians will I give over into the hand of a cruel lord; and a fierce king shall rule over them, saith the Lord, the Lord of hosts.” That is this administration right now, the fierce king of Daniel 8:23. Egypt in Joseph's day sold itself to Pharaoh for bread; the spiritual Egypt will be given over into the hand of a cruel lord.

precepts.text: The great city spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified: they crucify him in his image, his message and in denying that you men are the greatest thing on the earth.
precepts.point: I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: militia against militia, civil war, brother against brother, city against city. The stars are falling and the stripes are broken; this place is divided.
precepts.why:
“The burden of Egypt.” Egypt was before Isaiah’s time, so what Egypt is this speaking about? Revelation answers it: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

It says spiritually. Sodom is not around anymore; it is destroyed, those cities of Sodom and Gomorrah near Ein Bokek are nothing. But spiritual Sodom is here. It goes on even in the landmass of Israel among the Israelis, but prominently and predominately here in America, with all types of switcheroos: men acting like women and women acting like men, committing things contrary to the laws of God. And it is spiritual Egypt, the house of bondage. So replace Egypt with America: the burden of America.

“where also our Lord was crucified.” They crucify Christ in his image, in his message, and in denying that you men are the greatest thing on the face of this earth. They say, hell no, all people, God loves everybody.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city.” America is that great city, and our people are spiritually dead here. They are fearful of freedom; there is no spirit in them to rebel with the laws of God.

So when Isaiah says the Lord rides upon a swift cloud and comes into Egypt, it is the Lord coming with his chariots and angels to bring wrath and destruction upon America. Its idols shall be moved at his presence, and its heart, the mindset, doctrines and mentality of the oppressive kingdom, shall melt in the midst of it. He will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: militia against militia, civil war, brother against brother, city against city. This place is divided; the stars are falling and the stripes are broken. That is Esau rising against himself, and it is not our fight.

precepts.text: Blow the trumpet, sanctify a fast, gather the children and the sucklings, and let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, no more weddings, while the priests weep and say spare thy people, because our people are dying; then the Lord is jealous for his land, and removes far off the northern army into the land of Israel between the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean, where his stink comes up.
precepts.point: An altar to the Lord in the midst of Egypt, and an altar is for sacrifice, the Israelites; they cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he sends them a saviour and a great one, Christ, who delivers them, the same as Jeremiah 30:7.
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors.” What will the oppressors be doing? The same thing 2 Esdras 16, Revelation 12:17, Matthew 10 and Matthew 24 say: Jacob's trouble. Joel shows the crying.

“Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts.” This is going to be a major fast, because there will be so much devastation to our people. “Let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet”: when this fast goes out, we are not doing weddings or planning weddings. Weddings are finished. We have to pray to the Lord because our people are dying.

“Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord.” That is the cry of Isaiah 19, crying bitterly because there is going to be death. “And give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He answers, “I will send you corn, and wine, and oil” and “I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen: But I will remove far off from you the northern army.” That is the great multitude after us in 2 Esdras 16. He will “drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea.” The east sea is the Dead Sea and the utmost sea is the Mediterranean: the land of Israel between them, what they call the Middle East. The Lord is going to cause things to pop off there.

“And his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up, because he hath done great things.” The Lord is going to destroy them over there: tribulation, World War III, Armageddon. It is all laid out for us. Yes, you are dying, but you are not dead; the Lord takes the northern army down, and then he sends us “a saviour, and a great one”, Christ, to deliver us.

precepts.text: The counsel against Edom and Teman: the least of the flock, the fake Israelis, draws them out into that land, the earth is moved at the noise of their fall, heard in the Red Sea, and he comes up and flies as the eagle over Bozrah, Jordan, America to Israel's rescue, and the hearts of the mighty men of Edom are as a woman in her pangs, because it is a trap and NATO turns against them.
precepts.point: An altar to the Lord in the midst of Egypt, and an altar is for sacrifice, the Israelites; they cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he sends them a saviour and a great one, Christ, who delivers them, the same as Jeremiah 30:7.
precepts.why:
Joel says the Lord will remove the northern army far off and drive it into the land between the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean. Jeremiah shows what happens there.

“Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman.” Teman is still Edom. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: the least of the flock is these Israelis, the fake Israelis. That whole area on the map is where it is all going to go down. “Surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.”

“The earth is moved at the noise of their fall, at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea.” The ships in the Red Sea are going to hear about this fall.

“Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah.” Bozrah is Jordan, that area on the map. America is going to come to Israel's rescue, so they think. “And at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.” They are going to be afraid, because they don't realize it's a trap: NATO turns against them, and everybody is against America and Israel.

That is how the Lord takes the northern army down over there, while he tells us, don't worry, you are dying but you are not dead. Jacob's trouble is great, “but he shall be saved out of it.”

precepts.text: The Lord gathers one by one all ye children of Israel, and they come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria and the outcasts in the land of Egypt: that is who Egypt my people is.
precepts.point: Blessed be Egypt my people and Assyria the work of my hands: the one verse they might run to for another nation, and a few chapters on the Lord beats off from the stream of Egypt and gathers one by one the children of Israel, those ready to perish in Assyria and the outcasts in Egypt, to worship at Jerusalem. My people in Egypt and Assyria means Israel in those lands, the remnant recovered the second time from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar and Hamath, Judah and Joseph brought again out of Egypt and Assyria.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance.” That is the one verse they might run with: see, Egypt is his people and Assyria is his people, so the Egyptians and the Assyrians are saved too. No problem. Go over a few chapters and see where this Egypt and Assyria are.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel.” Gathered one by one: who? The children of Israel.

“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the great trumpet shall be blown”: that is Christ coming. “And they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt.” Earlier it said Egypt and Assyria; here it is the land of Assyria and the land of Egypt, and the ones coming out of them are the children of Israel. So who is “Egypt my people” and Assyria? Israelites.

“And shall worship the Lord in the holy mount at Jerusalem.” My people in Egypt and my people in Assyria means Israel in those lands, scattered there and gathered out one by one to worship at Jerusalem. That is how precepts work: you don't build a doctrine for another nation on one verse.

precepts.text: The remnant recovered the second time from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath and the islands of the sea.
precepts.point: Blessed be Egypt my people and Assyria the work of my hands: the one verse they might run to for another nation, and a few chapters on the Lord beats off from the stream of Egypt and gathers one by one the children of Israel, those ready to perish in Assyria and the outcasts in Egypt, to worship at Jerusalem. My people in Egypt and Assyria means Israel in those lands, the remnant recovered the second time from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar and Hamath, Judah and Joseph brought again out of Egypt and Assyria.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
Just in case Isaiah 27 is not enough, beat a dead horse. “And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people.” That is the same gathering we read in Isaiah 27.

From where? “Which shall be left, from Assyria”: my people. “And from Egypt”: Egypt, my people. “And from Pathros”: still Egypt, my people. “And from Cush, and from Elam”: Elam is Iran and Pakistan, my people. “And from Shinar”: Shinar is Iraq, my people. “And from Hamath”: Syria, my people. “And from the islands of the sea”: the islands, whether the Mediterranean or the Caribbean. That is his people.

It names Assyria and Egypt right there with the rest, and in every one of those places it is the remnant of his people that he recovers, not the nations of those lands. So when Isaiah 19 says “Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands”, it is speaking of Israel scattered in Egypt and Assyria, whom the Lord recovers the second time.

precepts.text: I will save the house of Joseph and bring them again, and they shall be as though I had not cast them off; I will hiss for them and gather them, and bring them again out of the land of Egypt and out of Assyria.
precepts.point: Blessed be Egypt my people and Assyria the work of my hands: the one verse they might run to for another nation, and a few chapters on the Lord beats off from the stream of Egypt and gathers one by one the children of Israel, those ready to perish in Assyria and the outcasts in Egypt, to worship at Jerusalem. My people in Egypt and Assyria means Israel in those lands, the remnant recovered the second time from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar and Hamath, Judah and Joseph brought again out of Egypt and Assyria.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
One more, just in case. “And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them again to place them.” Bring them again: that is the second time, the recovering of Isaiah 11. “For I have mercy upon them: and they shall be as though I had not cast them off”: as though they had never been in captivity. “For I am the Lord their God, and will hear them.”

“And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man, and their heart shall rejoice as through wine: yea, their children shall see it, and be glad.” “I will hiss for them, and gather them; for I have redeemed them.” Both Judah and Joseph, Judah and Ephraim: he will gather all twelve tribes. “And they shall increase as they have increased. And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries; and they shall live with their children, and turn again.”

“I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria.” Bring who again? All twelve tribes, out of Egypt and out of Assyria, the same as Isaiah 11:11. “And I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them.”

So what does “Egypt my people” and “Assyria the work of my hands” mean? It means Israel in those lands. That makes four scriptures, and there is no arguing with it. That is called precepts.

precepts.text: The Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit.
precepts.point: The Lord hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof. Egypt is spiritually America.
precepts.why:
“Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit.” That is the war of gods. On one side is the god still sitting in our minds, the image of white supremacy that was forced into our spirits; on the other side is the God of this Bible. The Egyptians set themselves up as gods, but they are only men, and all their weaponry is flesh.

Their weapons are not only for warring with other people. They are there to force a thought into our minds, to force white supremacy into our spirits. So the war is first in the mind, and the ignorance of our people is the battlefield.

“When the Lord shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together.” That is what Isaiah 19 shows: the Lord sets “the Egyptians against the Egyptians”, “city against city, and kingdom against kingdom”, and “the spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof.” There is going to be civil war, and there will be wars from outside as well.

And when it comes, “they shall seek to the idols, and to the charmers, and to them that have familiar spirits, and to the wizards.” They will cry out to the images they revered as gods, talking to those Jesus pieces, asking them to come save them. They will run back to the news outlets that lied for years, to Christianity, to every version of white supremacy. But men are not God, and none of it will hold them up.

So the Lord is teaching us war tactics, because there are going to be wars in the flesh. We have to keep strong in the war we already have in our spirit, knowing the ones who made themselves gods over us are only flesh.

precepts.text: The great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt.
precepts.point: The Lord hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof. Egypt is spiritually America.
precepts.why:
Revelation 11 shows everybody where Egypt is: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” This place, America, is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt. So when Isaiah says “I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians”, he is speaking of civil war in this land, city against city and kingdom against kingdom.

That is why Isaiah 19 goes on: “The Lord hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof: and they have caused Egypt to err in every work thereof.” God put a perverse spirit here, and it causes this place to be in error in everything it does. Everything that America does is in error, because there is a perverse spirit here.

You can see it in the news. Trump went to the Ford plant, a worker called him a pedophile protector, and he shot the man the bird and said “F you”. The man was suspended, and the union is fighting to get him off suspension. Somebody called out the perverse spirit, and even when they are shown their errors, they flip you the bird and make sure you lose your job.

So Sodom and Egypt is not a far-off place. It is the land we are in, and the land that the Lord will turn against itself.

precepts.text: The great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.
precepts.point: Egypt is America: spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, with Egypt's symbols on its dollar.
precepts.why:
“The burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord rideth upon a swift cloud, and shall come into Egypt: and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence.” The commentaries say this is about ancient times, but verse 1 lets you know it is future: the Lord coming into Egypt has not happened yet. So how do we know who this Egypt is?

Revelation tells us: “And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” The dead bodies are the Israelites, not literally dead but spiritually dead. The great city is Babylon the great, the United States of America. “which spiritually”: that is the key.

It is called Sodom because of the same-sex marriages, the transgenderism and all that filth in this country. It is not the real Sodom but a spiritual Sodom. And it is called Egypt: America knows its foundation is ancient Egypt. Look at the dollar bill: the pyramid, the all-seeing eye of Horus, 1776 at the bottom, Novus Ordo Seclorum, the New World Order, and the obelisk in Washington DC. America is aware that this is a spiritual Egypt; only the black and Latin Christians have not figured it out, and so they read the scriptures desperately confused.

“where also our Lord was crucified.” Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, but this is a spiritual crucifixion: they have crucified Christ’s image here and crucified his teachings here.

So Isaiah 19 is spiritual Egypt: “And I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.” Americans against Americans, a house divided: Democrats against Republicans, red cities against blue cities, white man against white man. There will be a civil war in this country.

precepts.text: They shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour.
precepts.point: The idle in the truth will be fed Christianity. Those two years or more in the congregation must examine themselves.
precepts.why:
“For, behold, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled over you”. Who is this great multitude that is over us? It is law enforcement, their military, set over the believing Israelites. Isaiah proves it.

“In that day shall there be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof”. This Egypt is a spiritual Egypt: America. An altar is used for sacrifice, so there is going to be a lot of death. “And it shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: for they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors”.

Why would we cry unto the Lord? Because of the oppressors, with an s on it: more than one. That is the great multitude whose burning wrath is kindled over us. That is Jacob's trouble, and we have not gotten to that part yet.

So the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16 is the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the power of spiritual Egypt that will be over our people in this land, and it is because of them that Israel will cry unto the Lord.

The spirit of Egypt fails in the midst of it, and He destroys the counsel thereof; they seek to the idols, the charmers, them that have familiar spirits, and the wizards.
The Egyptians are given over into the hand of a cruel lord, and a fierce king shall rule over them, saith the Most High of hosts.
The waters fail from the sea, the river is wasted and dried up, and the brooks of defense are emptied and dried up.
The reeds and flags wither, and everything sown by the brooks withers, is driven away, and is no more.
The fishers mourn, they that cast angle into the brooks and spread nets upon the waters lament and languish, and they that work in fine flax and weave networks are confounded.
The princes of Zoan are fools, and the counsel of the wise counselors of Pharaoh is become brutish.
They cannot tell Pharaoh what the Most High of hosts has purposed upon Egypt; the princes of Zoan are become fools and the princes of Noph are deceived.
The Most High has mingled a perverse spirit in the midst of Egypt and caused it to err in every work, as a drunken man staggers in his vomit.
There shall be no work for Egypt which the head or tail, branch or rush, may do.
In that day Egypt shall be like women, afraid because of the shaking of the hand of the Most High of hosts over it, and the land of Judah shall be a terror to Egypt.
Five cities in the land of Egypt shall speak the language of Canaan and swear to the Most High of hosts, and one shall be called the city of destruction.
In that day there shall be an altar to the Most High in the midst of the land of Egypt and a pillar at its border, for a sign and a witness to the Most High of hosts.
They shall cry to the Most High because of oppressors, and He shall send them a savior and a great one to deliver them; He shall smite Egypt and heal it as they return to Him.
In that day there shall be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria, and the Egyptians and the Assyrians shall serve together.
Israel shall be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, even a blessing in the midst of the land.

All of this is going into the scattered Israelites that are in Egypt and Assyria, whom the Most High of hosts blesses, saying, "Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of mine hands, and Israel mine inheritance."
